public_rationale: On March 7, 2024, RBC described U.S. equity valuations as above average and stretched, while stating that it did not consider the market a repeat of the technology bubble [e1]. RBC compared broad stock-market groups with earlier technology-bubble valuations [e1]. That analysis does not establish whether AI valuations and investment across the industry exceeded plausible economic returns in January–March 2024, or whether fundamentals justified them [e1].
limitations: The packet contains one analysis of public equities, with no comprehensive assessment of private AI investment or infrastructure commitments.
Lower valuation multiples than an earlier bubble do not establish fair value.
The claim defines neither a valuation threshold nor the set of AI companies and investments to assess.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: We are in an artificial intelligence bubble.

statement.excerpt: I've been hesitant to outright say that we're in an artificial intelligence bubble, or at least I was until I read that Microsoft and OpenAI are currently planning to build a $100 billion supercomputer dubbed "Stargate."

from_speaker: we're in an artificial intelligence bubble
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that speculation had pushed AI investment and valuations materially beyond plausible economic returns.
Use Q1 2024, the latest completed quarter before publication, to assess the ongoing market state.
The proposed Stargate expenditure is his reason for the conclusion, not a numerical definition of a bubble.
The claim does not predict a crash by any deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes widespread speculative overvaluation in AI during the target period, beyond what plausible earnings and growth expectations could justify.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes that the apparent industry-wide overvaluation was substantially explained by defensible economic fundamentals during the target period.

evidence.locator: Section Staying invested and vigilant, opening sentence
evidence.explanation: RBC describes valuations as stretched but argues that earnings, established businesses, and broader market participation distinguish the rally from the dot-com bubble. This is material contrary analysis, not proof of fair value across the AI industry.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An analysis of January–March 2024 AI valuations and investment commitments against contemporaneous earnings and plausible expected returns, covering a defined industry scope and using an explicit, defensible standard for speculative overvaluation.
